notes.made: Temperton wrote it and arranged the rhythm and vocals, and Getintothis credits him with giving the album its title too. Louis Johnson of the Brothers Johnson plays bass, John Robinson drums, Greg Phillinganes Rhodes and synth, and George Duke synthesizer, programming and sound effects alongside Michael Boddicker, with Paulinho da Costa on percussion and Jerry Hey's arrangement for the Seawind Horns. It was cut in December 1978 across Allen Zentz, Westlake and Cherokee in Los Angeles, with Swedien recording and mixing.
notes.context: The song is about leaving the working week behind for a night out, which suited a singer trying to get out from under his family's band. It came out as a single in the UK on 16 November 1979 and reached seven, and in the US on 31 January 1980, where it made ten on the Hot 100 and five R&B. That was the album's third US top ten; "She's Out of My Life" made the fourth, and no solo artist had done that before.

listen_for.where: the bass, all the way through
listen_for.note: Louis Johnson's line sits deep in the pocket and keeps the Heatwave-style bounce Temperton wrote into his grooves.

listen_for.where: the synth colors around the vocal
listen_for.note: Those are George Duke's, who is credited with synthesizer and sound effects on this track alone among Temperton's three.

leads_to.title: Strawberry Letter 23
leads_to.why: Quincy Jones produced the Brothers Johnson's take on Shuggie Otis's song two years before Off the Wall, and it went to number one R&B and five pop; it is the record that put Louis Johnson's band in Jones's orbit.

notes.unverified: I couldn't find a source describing the intro or placing George Duke's effects at a particular point in the song, so the second listening note stays general. Wikipedia says this song too was offered to Karen Carpenter first; left out for want of a first-hand source.

culture.title: Top ten on both sides
culture.line: Number seven in the UK and ten on the Hot 100, five on the R&B chart, and platinum in the US.

culture.title: Pete Rock, 1998
culture.line: Pete Rock sampled it for "Stay Away", with De La Soul and Rob-O, in 1998.

culture.title: Mariah Carey, 2008
culture.line: Mariah Carey interpolated it in "I'm That Chick" in 2008.
